messages.subject: Getting started with C++ section
parts:
From page 451 of the Stan manual (2.5.0):
Stan, unlike BUGS,
allows the user to directly program in C++, but we do not describe how to
do this in this Stan manual (see the getting started with C++ section of http:
//mc-stan.org for more information on using Stan directly from C++).

I cannot find the cited section in the main page! Could somebody please give me the direct link?

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Getting started with C++ section

Yes, RStan, PyStan and CmdStan are all examples.

There’s a pretty clean sampling and optimization
library, but they haven’t really been carefully designed
for use outside of Stan.

Let us know what your intended uses are, because
we’d like to refactor the code to make the C++
API useful.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Getting started with C++ section
parts:
Hi Bob,

 It would be nice if there is a tutorial how to use C++ API directly. For example, how to sample distribution A or hierarchy model B directly from C++ stan API.

   I have my own library to perform risk assessment. In risk assessment, several models require hierarchy bayesian analysis. In cmdstan, the output is written into csv file, but for a large model with many iterations, this becomes a bottleneck of performance. Then, I have to read csv file into memory to obtain posterior distributions. If my library directly access to C++ stan API and run simulation internally, I can remove unnecessary file IO to speedup.

Thanks,

Shota

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Getting started with C++ section
parts:
We're working on it. We're starting with the math and autodiff
lib, but then will probably go on to doc the rest of the API for
both developers and clients.

We haven't found I/O to be a bottleneck in any model we're interested
in. If the model's fast, the I/O time is trivial, if it's slow the
time is dominated by in-memory gradient calcs.

I could imagine if you need to run lots of little models it'd
make a difference, especially if they were running in parallel and
contending for disk/memory.

Have you benchmarked how much of the time is spent on I/O?

We originally designed RStan and PyStan to work directly
with memory, but I'm not sure it's a huge savings given how long
everything else takes.

- Bob

messages.author: ca51dc784e0edba6
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Getting started with C++ section
parts:
Hi Bob,

 Stan's IO is not slow compared with its computation time. However, R is not, for example. 
For convergence issues in my model, I need to run many iterations in parallel for many models. To process such data in R, rstan's read_stan_csv was too slow for me.

to save time, I did simple trick.
1. remove all unnecessary data from stan's output (with my own code).
2. read it into R via fread.
3. convert it to mcmc format.
4. do analysis

Anyway, I look forward to C++ API manual :)

Shota
